solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pursue and capture daughter in old German place

parts.note: Hun is an old, derogatory term for a German

indicators.note: the daughter is placed in the middle of the word for a place

parts.note: a town is a place

explanation.surface: A detective tracks a woman to a town in Germany to arrest her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside TOWN after its T, giving TDOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to chase someone persistently until they are caught.

clue.text: Hide empty sack at home

indicators.note: an empty sack has had its contents removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone stashes an empty sack somewhere in their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb about concealing; it is the noun, an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its pelt, a synonym.

clue.text: Look — old boy put up garden structure

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up writes it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Look at what the old fellow built in the garden!
explanation.definitionFit: A summerhouse or pavilion offering a view across a garden is exactly this.

clue.text: Law, say, broken repeatedly

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces and reassembled here in a new order

explanation.surface: A law, for instance, is broken over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something repeatedly is doing it constantly, every time.

clue.text: Firing about fifty for not working hard

indicators.note: the word for firing goes around the numeral

parts.note: sacking someone is firing them from a job
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty staff are being dismissed for idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SACKING around L, giving SLACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacking means idling or shirking, the opposite of working hard.

clue.text: Leave S. American capital: there's nothing to lose

indicators.note: the capital's name has to lose the letter for zero

parts.note: Quito is the capital of Ecuador
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A traveller decides to leave Ecuador's capital, having nothing to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place is to leave it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: On Chinese vessel man read out unwanted letters

parts.note: a junk is a traditional Chinese sailing ship

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for a man sounds like post

parts.note: a man is male

explanation.surface: A sailor on a Chinese ship reads out letters nobody wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited advertising post is junk mail, letters nobody asked for.

clue.text: Oaf included in school outing

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words school outing, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A clumsy boor was allowed on the school trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both oaf and lout mean a rough, clumsy, ill-mannered person.

clue.text: Heavy weight carried by expert without delay

indicators.note: the weight is held inside the word for an expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: A strong specialist lifts a heavy load immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, instantly, straight away.

clue.text: Coats manufactured in Berkshire town

indicators.note: manufactured goods are made up, so these letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: Coats are made in a town in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a town in Berkshire, west of London, famous for its royal horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse town in the English county of Berkshire.

clue.text: Youngster starts to behave, obeying you

indicators.note: the starts of the three words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A child starts to behave, doing as you say.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy is a male youngster, a young lad.

clue.text: Urban settlement so damp before start of October

parts.note: damp means wet

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the month is taken

explanation.surface: A town is so wet in the run-up to October.
explanation.walkthrough: SOWETO is a large township near Johannesburg, South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African township, a large urban settlement near Johannesburg.

clue.text: Former hospital worker and trader with contacts abroad

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a porter moves patients around a hospital

explanation.surface: A one-time hospital porter now does business overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who sells goods to foreign buyers has overseas contacts.

clue.text: Splutter, swallowing Irish rum perhaps

indicators.note: the word for splutter takes in the abbreviation

parts.note: to spit is to splutter

explanation.surface: Someone splutters after gulping Irish rum, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is one example of a distilled spirit, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: One church close to English port covered with frost

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England
Dover is a port on the English Channel

explanation.surface: A lone church near an English port lies under frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' is a link meaning next to; it does not pick a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface coated with frost or ice has frozen over completely.

clue.text: Rifleman runs after wading bird

indicators.note: runs comes after the bird, so it is written second

parts.note: a snipe is a long-billed wading bird
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rifleman goes after a bird in the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman firing a rifle from cover; the name comes from shooting snipe.

clue.text: Write name again and step down

definitions.meaning: put one's signature down once more

explanation.surface: An official signs a document again and leaves office.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-sign it means sign again; read whole it means quit a post.

clue.text: Caught bad egg misbehaving

indicators.note: letters that misbehave do not stay in their proper order

explanation.surface: A troublemaker was caught behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagging something is catching it, as a hunter bags game.

clue.text: Motorcyclist goes round about, making row

indicators.note: the motorcyclist word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a biker rides a motorcycle
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A biker circling about causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is the quarrel sense, rhyming with cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to quarrel pettily, a synonym of the verb to row.

clue.text: Fellow first out of grocery store

indicators.note: the store's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a deli sells groceries and cooked meats

explanation.surface: A man is the first to leave the grocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli serves as a typical man's name, so it can stand for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword convention: a male first name may be clued as a man or fellow.

clue.text: Strongholds frost damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Castles were damaged by frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortified buildings are strongholds, places built for defence.

clue.text: Dull place to live

definitions.meaning: a set of rooms on one floor, an apartment

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is lacking interest; the other is a British apartment.

clue.text: Keep transporting cardboard box

definitions.meaning: keep carting, carry on moving goods
a light container made of card

explanation.surface: Someone keeps lugging a cardboard box around.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as cart on it means continue carrying; whole it is a packing container.

clue.text: Line of soldiers fled, pursued by king

parts.note: ran means fled
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A line of soldiers ran away with the king chasing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers standing side by side form a rank, a row.

clue.text: Wild party in Gravesend

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the town name

explanation.surface: A wild party takes place in Gravesend.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town in Kent on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large lively dance party, a wild party.

clue.text: Knitted sweater for a milk supplier

definitions.meaning: a thick woollen fisherman's jumper from the Channel Islands
a breed of dairy cow from the Channel Islands

explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Island gives its name both to a knitted jumper and to a dairy cow breed.
